description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: go looking for reflections in puddles after the rain and draw what the water shows you.

body.heading: Wait for the rain to stop
paragraphs: Puddle hunting starts after the rain. Put on your wellies and walk slowly with your adult. Look down at the ground and search for still, shiny puddles.
A calm puddle works like a mirror. You might see the sky, a tree, a house, or your own smiling face looking back at you.

body.heading: Look closely
paragraphs: Stand very still and watch the reflection. What colours can you see? Now drop one tiny pebble at the edge and watch the picture wobble and dance.
Try looking from a different spot. Does the picture in the puddle change when you move? Reflections love to play tricks.

body.heading: Remember your favourite
paragraphs: Choose the puddle you liked best. Try to fix the picture in your mind like a photograph.
When you get home, you can draw it. Wobbly lines are perfect — puddle pictures are wobbly in real life too.

takeaway: A still puddle is a free mirror made by the rain, and it shows the world upside down.
safetyNotes: Only walk in puddles an adult says are safe, away from roads. Wash your hands when you come back inside.
screenFreeExtension: Draw your favourite puddle picture from memory at the table and see how much you can remember.
